caseno: Criminal Miscellaneous Case Nos. 7339 of 2003 and 7688 of 2003
lawyer:
Anisul Huq and Md Khurshid Alam Khan, Advocates—For the Petitioners. 
Sheikh Abdul Awal, Deputy Attorney-General with SM Aminul Islam, Assistant Attorney-General—For the Opposite Party-State.
parties:
Nasim (Md) and another ------ Petitioners
vs
State ------ Opposite Party
full_judgment:
SM Dastagir Husain J: These two Rules involving identical, similar facts are disposed of by this judgment. The petitioners Mohammad Nasim in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 7339/03 and the petitioner MK Bazlur Rahman in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 7688 of 2003 have moved an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashment of the proceeding initiated under Metropolitan Special Case No. 101/2002 arising out of Ramna Police Station Case No. 65(6)02 under sections 418 /109 of the Penal Code and section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act pending in the Court of the learned Metropolitan Senior Special Judge, Dhaka. 

 2. The first information report was lodged by Officer, Anti-Corruption Bangladesh, Dhaka on 19-6-2002 with the Ramna Police Station alleging, inter alia, that the former Minister of Post & Telecommunication Md Nasim in collusion with the petitioner of another Miscellaneous Case MK Bazlur Rahman who was President, Bangladesh Broadcasting Telephone Technology (hereinafter to be referred as BBTT) in collusion with each other and with dishonest intention signed licensing agreement for establishing 2,00,000 PHS Telephone in Dhaka City with BBTT. The petitioner Md Nasim has misused his power as Minister of Government of Bangladesh and signed an agreement which is against the interest of the Government, as such, both the petitioners committed an offence under sections 418/409 of the Penal Code and section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act. It was further stated in the first information report that Mr MK Bazlur Rahman, President, BBTT on 13-8-1997 submitted an unsolicited proposal to Mr Md Nasim, Minister of Post and Telecommunication for a licence to set up 2,00,000 Personal Handy Phone system in Dhaka City the revenue of which will be shared by Bangladesh Government and BBTT on 51% and 49% basis. On receipt of the said proposal the former Minister sent it to the Bangladesh Telephone and Telegraph Board for evaluation and Bangladesh Telephone and Telegraph Board (hereinafter to be referred as T&T Board) opined that this proposal is less attractive than that of cellular operators and the technical financial and management capability of BBTT needs to be thoroughly examined. Later, on 29-7-1998 at a meeting presided over by Mr Md Nasim, it was decided that the proposal should be sent to the Cabinet Sub-Committee of Finance and Economic Affairs within seven days. Md Nasim also directed that a summary be prepared to be placed before the Sub-Committee. When the summary was placed before the Secretary of the said Ministry SD Khan on 29-12-1998, he objected to the said proposal and further opined that tender be floated for the implementation of the project. In his note the Secretary, observed that the PHS system should be introduced on a build, own and operate (BOO) system for which international tender should be called or an advertisement be published in the local newspapers inviting offers for comparative proposals. But this note of the Secretary was disregarded by the Minister and after preparation of summary the proposal was sent to the cabinet sub-committee on finance and economic affairs and on 2-3-1999 the Cabinet Sub-Committee approved the proposal with the observation that credential, reliability, goodwill, efficiency and financial arrangement of the proposal should be examined by the Secretary, External Resources Division and Bangladesh Bank. It is further stated that if the External Resources Division and Bangladesh Bank are satisfied with the proposal then it should be implemented. On 17-10-1999 Mr Nazrul Islam, Joint Secretary of Post and Telecommunication, made a proposal to hold meeting under the Chairmanship of Md Nasim, the Minister for Post and Telegraph with the Governor, Bangladesh Bank and Secretaries of ERD and Post & Telecommunication Ministry and the Chairman of T&T Board to evaluate the offer in the light of the opinion of the Cabinet Sub-Committee on Finance and Economic Affairs. The Secretary of this Ministry, approved' the note of the Joint Secretary and sent it to the Ministry but Md Nasim, to fulfil his dishonest intention, gave a direction that Mr MK Bazlur Rahman be called for direct discussion with the ministry. Thereafter, a note was prepared for a direction as to whether the contract should be signed even though no opinion was received from the Bangladesh Bank or External Resources Division. But Ex-Minister Mr Nasim totally disregarded the opinion of the officials of the Ministry and ordered signing of the agreement. Therefore, it is evident from his conduct that Md Nasim in collusion with Mr Bazlur Rahman, with dishonest intention and by abusing official power, signed a licensing agreement which was detrimental to the financial interest of the country and by doing so committed an offence under sections 418/109 of the Penal Code and section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act. 

 5. Mr Md Anisul Huq, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of Mohammad Nasim, the petitioner in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 7339 of 2003 and Mr Md Khurshed Alam Khan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of MK Bazlur Rahman, the petitioner in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 7688 of 2003, submit that from the plain reading of the first information report story it does not reveal delivery of any property belonging to anybody through fraud and dishonesty by the petitioners and also the allegations made in the first information report cannot constitute an offence under section 418 of the Penal Code or under section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act and no offence of cheating as defined in section 415 as made out and attracts section 418 of the Penal Code, as such, the question of appreciation of evidence does not arise in this case. Further, they submit that in the first information report there is no allegation of pecuniary benefit obtained by the petitioners, as such, from the first information report itself no case of cheating or unholy gain stands. Moreover, nowhere it is mentioned that according to the instruction of former Minister such opinion was given such admitted position that the petitioner has neither cheated the Government nor delivered any property of the Government which has caused loss to the Government, as such, its prolongation will be the abuse of the process of the court which requires to be quashed. 

 6. On the other hand, the learned Deputy Attorney-General, appearing on behalf of the opposite party, State, by filing counter-affidavit, submits that there are sufficient materials available. disclosing a strong prima facie case for believing that the accused petitioners had direct complicity/overt act in the commission or the offence under sections 418/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947. The police after thorough investigation into the matter submitted charge-sheet against the accused petitioners and others, specially on the basis of documentary evidences which can be determined only on taking evidence at the trial. Therefore, the instant proceeding cannot be quashed at this stage. Further, he submits that a prima facie case has been established from the said first information report and the charge-sheet. The offences against the petitioners are economic offence against the State and society as a whole attracting a clear prima facie offence under section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 and, as such, the proceeding cannot be quashed and the Rule is liable to be discharged. The learned Deputy Attorney General by referring 1 BLC 446 submits that the petitioners by abusing their official power made a contract and in the light of the said decision it can only be determined by evidences in the trial. But the decision as referred above is with regard to purchase by abusing official power but in this case a contract was signed and yet it is to be acted upon. Therefore, it requires no inquiry as to whether the allegation is reliable or not and, as such, the decision cited is distinguishable with the present case. Further, he refers 1 BLC (AD) 169 wherein it has been stated as follows: 

 "It is well known that guilty intention as an ingredient of an offence is required to be proved by evidence and circumstances at the trial and this matter cannot be considered for quashing the proceeding under section 561A CrPC. It is enough that allegations are there in the petition of complaint constituting the alleged offence about which there is no doubt in the present case." 

 7. It is also distinguishable as because the case is with regard to fraudulent transfer but in the present case this is with regard to a contract and the contract are still to be acted upon. 

 Moreover, there is no mention of pecuniary benefit out of the said contract against the petitioners. Therefore, the instant case is also not applicable. The guilty intention is absent in the present case. Thereafter, the learned Deputy Attorney-General further referred 5 BLC 662 wherein in the said reported case the accused persons made arrangement of printing additional receipt books with dishonest motive of monetary gain to themselves by abusing their official position as public servants. But in this case the petitioners' dishonest motive or intention to get any pecuniary benefit out of the contract have been said in the said first information report by abusing their official position as public servants, as such, the decision is distinguishable with the present case. Lastly, he submits by referring 1994 BLD (AD) 161 wherein it has been stated as follows: 

 This decision is also not applicable as the charge has not yet been framed in this particular case. In the same 1994 BLD (AD) 206 wherein it has been stated as follows: 

 "Even though a Minister is found to be personally interested in a criminal case against the accused appellant yet this, by itself, is not sufficient to conclude that the specific allegations against the appellant are false. The High Court Division was right in holding that the question of malafiaes could be determined only on taking evidence at the trial and was justified in refusing to quash the proceeding." 

 In this particular case, the minister even if found that he has directed to make the agreement without taking any opinion from BBTT or from Bangladesh Bank or even if it is taken that there is a specific allegation but that does not come within the definition of section 415 of the Penal Code. The question of malafides does not come within the definition clause of section 415 of Penal the Code. The section says as follows: 

 "Any public servant who commits or attempts to commit criminal misconduct shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both and the pecuniary resources or property to which the criminal misconduct relates may also be confiscated to the State." 

 9. In this particular case, there is no appearance of dishonesty, fraudulent activities, misappropriation, corruption by illegal means or otherwise abusing official position as public servant obtained any valuable pecuniary advantage are being stated in the said first information report, as such, we find substance in the Rule for quashment of the proceeding. The petitioner MK Bazlur Rahman is a contractor who has placed the proposal which may be accepted or that may be rejected and this proposal is not coming within the ambit of sections 418/109 and 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act. Therefore, we find it difficult to accept the contention of the learned Deputy Attorney-General that there are ingredients for which the proceeding should not be quashed. Under these facts and circumstances as stated above, we are inclined to quash the proceeding. The impugned proceeding initiated under Metropolitan Special Case No. 101 of 2002 arising out of Ramna PS Case No. 65(6) 2002 under sections 418/109 of the Penal Code and section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 pending in the Court of learned Metropolitan Senior Special Judge, Dhaka is thereby quashed. Accordingly, both the Rules are made absolute.
